finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete() but ignores the boolean result, so the authorization check is never enforced. Any caller can delete any account.
finding.source: Any authenticated user calling DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary id (the id is attacker-controlled).
finding.sink: accounts.remove(id) at line 23, the protected delete operation.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) is the entry point for DELETE /accounts/{id}.
The account is fetched by the attacker-supplied id with no ownership scoping.
canDelete(u, a) returns a boolean that is discarded. It does not throw.

finding.guards_checked: canDelete is a pure predicate that does not throw, and its result is unused here. closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete, which throws, but deleteAccount does not. No other authorization layer is visible in the file.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (line 9) is a pure boolean predicate; its result is discarded at line 22. assertCanDelete (line 13) throws but is only used in closeAccount (line 29). No other callers or auth layers exist in the directory.
verdict.reason: src/AccountService.java:22 calls canDelete as a bare statement with the boolean discarded, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated user, whereas closeAccount at line 29 correctly uses the throwing assertCanDelete.
